Subject: Deal thresholds & capacity checkpoint — weekly triage

Team —

Quick agenda for today's capacity checkpoint (30 min):
- Review Clearwave AI (CW-4821) forecast vs commit thresholds
- Confirm reservation tiers + burst window for demo week (Dec 6–10)
- Action owners for infra provisioning + contract milestones

Attached: pipeline_snapshot_Q4.csv (high-level forecast), infra_capacity_estimate.xlsx (initial slot math).

Notes / asks:
1) Laura — can you confirm the % conversion assumptions you used for the forecast table? The HubSpot numbers look optimistic and I want us to align on threshold triggers for the dedicated reserve.
2) Ben/Jordan — from infra: please confirm whether we can guarantee an extra 12 A100-equivalent slots for the demo week without impacting other reserve deals. If not, propose alternatives (burst credits, canary routing).
3) Kimberly — finance: we may need a short-term credit holdback for the first 30 days if they sign with lower-than-expected ARR; can you advise on precedent?

Going to pull this into today's 10:00 standup; if you can't make it, reply with your gating concerns.

Thanks —
Jonas
--

Jonas —

Thanks for the pull. Quick answers:
- Forecast assumptions: using HubSpot pipeline stage velocity + conversion = 18% close rate across Q4 for ACV-tiered deals. I put a conservative scenario tab in the CSV with 9% lower case for worst-case planning.
- Demo week: marketing told me the customer will run 2 high-concurrency sessions; we should plan for peak concurrency ~60k tokens/min for those days.

I'll be on the 10:00. If we need to tighten thresholds, recommend trigger at 55% of the 90-day pipeline forecast to recommend moving to dedicated reserve negotiations.

Laura

Subject: Re: Deal thresholds & capacity checkpoint — weekly triage

Jonas / Laura —

Short infra readout after reviewing infra_capacity_estimate.xlsx:
- Baseline: we have 96 reserved A100-equivalent slots across current contracts; typical steady-state buffer is ~18 slots.
- Impact: supporting Clearwave demo week (peak concurrency described by Laura) requires ~12 additional A100-equivalent slots for five days to keep p99 latency under 350ms with current batching. That matches your ask.
- Options:
  1) Temporarily shift 12 slots from low-priority sprint pools (risk: may degrade non-enterprise batch jobs)
  2) Offer a compensated burst credit package (preferred short-term; no infra-side churn)
  3) Canary routing + quantized model variant for demo (reduces slot need to ~6)

Recommendation: we propose option 2 for sales-facing conversations (fastest to commit) while engineering validates option 3 as a fallback. I'll attach a short workbook with cost delta scenarios.

Ben

Ben Carter

Jonas / team —

Thanks for the quick coordination. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Demo week concurrency: marketing will run a 2-hour demo on Dec 8 with partners, expect extra load between 10:00–12:00 PT. We can stagger some sessions if needed but prefer minimal impact to demonstration quality.
- Procurement: we've routed the signed NDA (attached) and procurement will need the standard SOW + a confirmed estimate of peak slots + estimated monthly spend to process PO.

If you can confirm a recommended path (burst credits vs temporary slots) by EOD Monday, procurement will prioritize the PO queue.

Best,
Emma
